instructions:
### ROLE ###
You maintain a small, growing set of CONCEPT SCHEMES (entity categories) for a knowledge registry built from cybersecurity incident reports. A group of entities extracted from several reports has just been found to be close to each other and far from every existing scheme. Decide whether the group is a genuinely new scheme or an alias of an existing one, and name it.

### EXISTING SCHEMES ###
- Software Product: A software application, plugin, utility, or platform developed for end users or computing infrastructure.
- Security Advisory: An official public notice issued by an organization detailing cybersecurity vulnerabilities, patches, or mitigation recommendations.
- Security Vulnerability: A flaw or weakness in software, firmware, or hardware that can be exploited to compromise system security.
- Operating System: System software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for computer programs.
- Country: A distinct sovereign nation, state, or recognized territorial entity with defined borders and governance.
- Government Agency: An official state department, ministry, or public authority exercising governmental administration and functions.
- Malware: Software, scripts, or malicious files designed to compromise, disrupt, damage, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems.

### THE GROUP ###
Each line is one entity with the description written at extraction time:
- January 2020 Security Updates [software update] — A collection of security patches released by Microsoft on January 15, 2020.
- WP Dataset Reset 3.15 [software update] — A patched release of the WP Database Reset plugin that addresses security vulnerabilities.
- KB4014793 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Windows Vista and Windows Server 2008.
- KB3141529 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Office 2007 addressing security vulnerabilities.
- KB3178703 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Office 2016 addressing security vulnerabilities.
- KB3178710 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Office 2013 addressing security vulnerabilities.
- KB3141538 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Office 2010 addressing security vulnerabilities.
- KB4015549 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Windows 7 addressing security vulnerabilities.
- KB4015546 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Windows 7 addressing security vulnerabilities.
- KB4015551 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Windows Server 2012 addressing vulnerabilities.
- KB4015548 [software update] — A Microsoft security update for Windows Server 2012 addressing vulnerabilities.

### RULES ###
- A scheme is a KIND of entity (e.g. "Hacker group", "Malware family", "Software product", "Government body", "Internet domain", "Country"), never a role in an incident and never a single entity.
- Return `"verdict": "alias-of"` with `"target"` set to an existing scheme's label when the group is the same kind as that scheme (different wording, same meaning). Judge by MEANING of the descriptions, not by surface words.
- Return `"verdict": "new"` when no existing scheme covers the group. Then give:
  - `prefLabel`: a short English noun phrase, 1–3 words, singular, Title Case (e.g. "Malware Family").
  - `definition`: one sentence, at most 25 words, stating what belongs to the scheme, general enough to hold across reports.
  - `altLabels`: 0–3 alternative English labels.
- If the group mixes clearly different kinds, name the kind of the MAJORITY and list the minority entity names in `outliers`.
- If uncertain between alias and new, prefer `new`: an extra scheme can be merged later; a wrong merge cannot be undone cheaply.

### OUTPUT ###
A single raw JSON object, no markdown fences, no commentary:
{ "verdict": "new" | "alias-of", "target": "<existing label or null>", "prefLabel": "...", "definition": "...", "altLabels": [...], "outliers": [...] }
text: Decide and name the group now.
response: {"verdict": "new", "target": null, "prefLabel": "Software Update", "definition": "A software release, patch, or package designed to fix vulnerabilities, address bugs, or update existing programs.", "altLabels": ["Security Patch", "Software Patch", "Security Update"], "outliers": []}
